status: Windows-only source/evidence review; no execution, new allocation matrix, protocol change or candidate retention

supplements.rule: The original checklist is preserved byte-for-byte. This additive document distinguishes logical storage, retained allocations and transient memory.

definitions.logical_storage: Centroid count/element size, wire length and exact serialized contents. These do not measure a Vec's spare capacity, allocator size class or process memory.
definitions.retained_capacity: Actual Vec capacity, or an ndarray's public owned payload shape/dtype/nbytes; these are separate representations and should be named precisely.
definitions.retained_requested_and_usable: For the instrumented Jemalloc studies, live allocation bytes at return minus live bytes after result drop. Requested layout bytes and backend usable size are separately recorded.
definitions.boundary_peak: Instrumented live bytes observed at GlobalAlloc boundaries. This excludes allocator-internal realloc overlap, native allocations bypassing this allocator and RSS.
definitions.static_no_growth: An unchanged retained-output construction/compaction path can support a structural no-growth conclusion; it is not an empirical allocator count, usable-byte or peak-memory measurement.

E02.source_assessment: The helper borrows the same ordered centroid runs and retains the existing result construction/compression. Owned merge_digests remains an owned API. In-place merge and merge_many stop cloning input digests; the replacement digest follows the same allocation/compaction path. The temporary runs Vec uses the exact lower size hint for the actual array/slice/once-chain callers, replacing the old owned-vector length. No extra storage is retained in TDigest.
E02.remaining: No dedicated allocation matrix is needed merely to establish unchanged retained representation. Bind this source argument to the final patch/manifests during integration. Say avoids input clones, not measured peak RSS reduction. Actual allocator-byte claims would require separate evidence and are not currently proposed.

E03.source_assessment: Only the two-nonempty-run producer changes. TwoWayCentroidMerge stores two borrowed slices and returns the same exact sequence and remaining length; both branches feed unchanged compress_into and result construction. It removes the temporary heap for this branch, without adding retained digest fields or a new output allocation policy.
E03.remaining: Structural retained-allocation argument is sufficient for this unchanged output path; retain the existing public-shape gate. Do not infer an empirical peak or exact allocation savings from source inspection. No extra capacity grid is warranted.

E08.remaining: Use the source-based retained no-growth argument and scheduled exact public-shape audit. No new allocation matrix is needed. Do not convert this into a claim of observed peak/RSS reduction.

E12.source_assessment: PyArray1::from_slice copies the existing f64 result into NumPy-owned storage, removing intermediate Python list/float boxing. It does not transfer Rust Vec spare capacity to the ndarray. TDigest state and core vectors are unchanged; list/tuple/scalar routes retain their established behavior.
E12.remaining: Returned-output ownership and payload no-growth evidence is already adequate; no new allocation grid is required for this candidate. State the concrete removed boxing/copy path and equal NumPy payload, without claiming a quantified allocator or peak-memory saving. Recheck applicable ownership/compatibility on the final installed artifact.

E20.source_assessment: The new branch uses the existing prefix Vec and an allocation-free forward cursor. Its result uses slice iter().map().collect() with exact length, replacing the scalar branch's Vec::with_capacity(vals.len()) and pushes. No digest state is retained or changed. The allocator policy is structurally bounded to the same output length, but exact returned capacity has not been recorded.
E20.remaining: If E20 survives speed gates, a small public Vec len/capacity check using existing target/fallback boundary requests is the only useful extra no-growth witness; this needs no production instrumentation or timing. Propose it as an additive validation-only check, not an altered frozen216-case report or a new broad allocation matrix. Do not label the currently unmeasured capacity or peaks as observed.
